about: Tooltips the report viewer (reports/view.html, reports/tips.js) puts on report labels that are explained here rather than in the finance glossary (Oki, 10 Oct 2026). tools/glossary.py checks every common label has a glossary entry or a tip. match: exact (default), prefix or contains; in: CSS selector the label must sit in; term: the finance glossary entry to link, required when the glossary also covers the label.

labels.label: Static data as of
labels.tip: Every figure on this page is frozen at this date, usually a market close or the publisher's latest release. Nothing updates until the report is refreshed.

labels.label: Mkt Cap Ranking
labels.tip: Rank by stock-market value, #1 the largest. For S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100 members it is our own count on this page's date; companies based abroad often show a home-market rank.

labels.label: Next Earnings
labels.tip: When the company is next due to report results, and for which quarter. A ~ or est. means the company had not confirmed the date when this page was built.

labels.label: Metric
labels.tip: Each row is one ratio: the company's figure, a typical industry figure, the index figure, then context. ~ approximate, est. estimate, n/m not meaningful, n/v no verified value, — none.

labels.label: Industry Avg
labels.tip: A typical value of the same ratio among companies in the same business. It is approximate, each report picks its own peers, and a dash means no comparable figure.

labels.label: S&P 500
labels.tip: The ratio for the whole S&P 500 treated as one company, built from our reports on every member and weighted by market value. A dash means no fair index figure.

labels.label: Nasdaq-100
labels.tip: The ratio for the whole Nasdaq-100 treated as one company, built from our reports on every member and weighted by market value. A dash means no fair index figure.

labels.label: Context
labels.tip: A note on what drives each figure, what distorts it and how it compares. Read it before comparing numbers; it often names a better measure for this business.

labels.label: 52-Week Range
labels.tip: The lowest and highest values over the past year. Where this page's figure sits between them shows how far it is off the high or up from the low.

labels.label: Rating Breakdown
labels.tip: How many analysts rate the stock at each step from Strong Buy to Strong Sell. The same consensus word can hide a united view or a split one.

labels.label: Target Range
labels.tip: The lowest and highest price targets among the analysts covering the stock. A wide range means they disagree sharply about where the price is heading.
